outline.title: 停电后的天文馆 / The Planetarium After the Storm
outline.summary: 暴雨让社区天文馆的控制系统停止工作。Noah、Ms. Rivera、Mina和管理员Dr. Hall没有冒险强行启动设备，而是根据记录、实时读数、已经完成的修复和安全要求逐步排查。团队为传感器测试准备了现实方案和备用方案，最终安全打开穹顶并按时举行活动。

chapters.title: 控制室上锁 / The Locked Control Room
chapters.summary: Noah和Ms. Rivera来到社区天文馆准备晚上的开放活动，却发现控制室被锁住，主电源也在暴雨后停止工作。Noah在旧值班记录中找到备用钥匙的位置，Ms. Rivera联系管理员Dr. Hall确认安全流程，两人进入控制室并发现一只被水浸湿的保险盒。
chapters.knowledgePointRecommendationSummary: Use Past simple to narrate the completed discovery and entry into the control room.

chapters.title: 控制台上的信号 / Signals on the Console
chapters.summary: 控制台重新通电后，指示灯不断闪烁，穹顶却仍然不动。Noah观察此刻正在变化的电压读数，Ms. Rivera对照设备平时的运行规则，发现冷却风扇现在没有转动。两人决定先处理风扇，而不是强行启动穹顶。
chapters.knowledgePointRecommendationSummary: Contrast actions happening now with the console's normal operating behaviour.

chapters.title: 已经完成的修复 / What the Team Has Repaired
chapters.summary: 同学Mina带来干燥工具，三人清理保险盒并重新连接风扇。Noah逐项汇报团队已经完成的修复和仍未解决的问题；Ms. Rivera根据这些最新结果判断主系统可以进入低功率测试，但穹顶传感器仍需要检查。
chapters.knowledgePointRecommendationSummary: Use Present perfect for completed repairs whose results matter to the current test.

chapters.title: 安全测试 / The Safety Test
chapters.summary: Dr. Hall远程说明安全要求：测试前必须清空穹顶轨道，所有人必须站在黄色线外，Noah还需要确认紧急停止按钮。团队逐项完成要求，随后发现一把维修梯仍挡在轨道旁，于是暂停测试并把它移走。
chapters.knowledgePointRecommendationSummary: Use have to and must for external safety requirements and strong necessary actions.

chapters.title: 如果穹顶打开 / If the Dome Opens
chapters.summary: 正式测试前，Noah比较现实方案和假设方案：如果传感器通过，他们就按原计划开放天文馆；如果传感器仍然失败，他们会把活动改成小型星图课。传感器最终通过，穹顶顺利打开，团队保留星图课作为备用方案并按时迎接参观者。
chapters.knowledgePointRecommendationSummary: Use real and hypothetical if-clauses to compare the available plans without changing the confirmed outcome.

args.title: 控制室上锁 / The Locked Control Room
args.cleanText: After the storm, Noah and Ms. Rivera arrived at the community planetarium to prepare for the evening event. The control-room door remained locked, and the main power was off. Instead of forcing the door, Noah checked the old duty records. He carefully examined each page and found a note about a spare key. The note directed them to a locked drawer near the front desk. Ms. Rivera called Dr. Hall, who confirmed the safe entry procedure. Noah collected the spare key, and they entered the control room together. Inside, they noticed water around a soaked fuse box, so they stopped and recorded the damage before touching anything.

args.title: 控制台上的信号 / Signals on the Console
args.cleanText: After the fuse box dried, the console received power again. Its lights flashed, but the dome stayed still. Noah watched the voltage display and said, “Look—the reading is changing right now, and the warning light is blinking now.” Ms. Rivera replied, “The system normally needs a steady voltage before the dome motor starts.” They compared the live readings with the operating guide. Noah pointed to the cooling unit. “The fan usually runs whenever the console operates, but it is not turning at the moment.” Ms. Rivera agreed that the heat could damage the system. They paused the test and marked the unusual signal. “Right now, we are choosing to repair the fan instead of forcing the dome open.”

args.title: 已经完成的修复 / What the Team Has Repaired
args.cleanText: Mina arrived with drying cloths, a small blower, and safe electrical tools. Following the recorded steps, the three cleaned the wet fuse box and reconnected the cooling fan. When the fan began turning, Noah reported, “So far, we have removed the water, and Mina has secured the loose cable. The console has shown a stable reading for several minutes.” Noah continued, “We have cleared the warning light, but we have not checked the dome sensor yet.” Ms. Rivera studied these latest results rather than guessing. “The repairs have made the main system safer,” she said. “So far, we have gathered enough evidence for a low-power test, but the sensor remains an unresolved issue.” They recorded every repair and prepared the testing area.

args.title: 安全测试 / The Safety Test
args.cleanText: Through a video call, Dr. Hall explained the safety requirements without doing the work for them. “Before testing, you have to clear the entire dome track,” he said. “Everyone must stand behind the yellow line, and Noah has to confirm the emergency stop button.” The team understood that these checks had to be completed before any movement. Mina inspected one side of the track while Noah checked the other. Ms. Rivera noticed a maintenance ladder beside the rail. “We must pause the test,” Noah said. “The ladder has to be moved first.” Together, the students carried it to the storage room and checked the track again. Before they could begin the low-power safety test, they had to check the track one final time.

args.title: 如果穹顶打开 / If the Dome Opens
args.cleanText: Before the final test, Noah compared their practical plan with a less likely situation. “If the sensor passes, we will open the planetarium as planned,” he said. “If it fails again tonight, we will hold a small star-map lesson instead. If we had more repair time, we would examine every wire, but visitors are arriving soon.” Ms. Rivera kept the star maps ready. The team started the test behind the yellow line. The sensor reading stayed steady, and the dome opened smoothly. “If we ignored the evidence, we would risk the equipment,” Noah said. Their result showed that if a team follows every safety step, it reduces the risk. They welcomed visitors on time. If the sensor failed later, they would use the star-map lesson as their backup plan.
